extras.description: Modal jazz (codified 1958-1965 through Miles Davis's Kind of Blue and John Coltrane's My Favorite Things and A Love Supreme establishing the works), the jazz subgenre built on improvisation over modes rather than chord-progressions. Distinguished from bebop by mode-not-chord-changes foundation; distinguished from later free jazz by retention of explicit-tonal center and metric pulse; distinguished from cool jazz by modal-not-arrangement focus.

extras.description: An instrumental genre built from the mid-1970s around meditation, healing and relaxation contexts rather than concert or dance use, spanning synthesizer suites, solo acoustic playing and world-instrument pastiche. source.lineage: Guitar-and-voice troubadour practice of eastern Cuba from the 1880s, carried by Santiago cantadores such as Pepe Sánchez, Sindo Garay, Manuel Corona and Rosendo Ruiz into Havana's patios and cafés: two singers in parallel thirds and sixths over one strummed and one arpeggiating guitar, moderate 2/4 or 6/8, bolero, criolla, guaracha and canción forms, decorated with punteo interludes and light claves or maracas.

extras.description: The itinerant guitar-song tradition of eastern Cuba, formed in Santiago in the 1880s and spread by singing troubadours who accompanied themselves and worked in duos singing close parallel harmony. The texture is deliberately thin — one guitar strums the rhythmic base while a second picks countermelodic punteo lines — with claves or maracas at most, and the repertoire runs across bolero, criolla, guaracha and patriotic canción. It is the parent stock of both the bolero cubano and the later nueva trova, distinguished from them by its unamplified courtyard scale, its authorship by singer-composers, and its complete absence of arrangement.

extras.description: A Ukrainian sung-epic practice carried by blind mendicant bandurists from the Cossack era until the tradition's near-destruction under Stalin, then rebuilt as a conservatory and capella art. extras.description: Swedish fiddle tradition is the regional dance-tune practice of Dalarna, Hälsingland, Jämtland and beyond, carried by named spelmän and since 1908 by the annual spelmansstämma gatherings. The core is the polska, a triple-time couple dance whose beats are unequal in ways specific to each parish, played with drone double-stops and an improvised second-fiddle harmony line. It is distinguished from Norwegian slått playing by its more even but still lilting polska, its ensemble stämma harmony practice, and its greater use of the nyckelharpa alongside the violin.
